title: Sex Differences in Hypertension in Older Adults: Role of Nitric Oxide
official: Sex Differences in Hypertension in Older Adults: Role of Nitric Oxide
summary:
The goal of this mechanistic clinical trial is to define nitric oxide-dependent mechanisms for sex-specific autonomic dysregulation in older adults with hypertension. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Whether nitric oxide bioavailability modulates peripheral sympathetic adrenergic control during orthostatic stress? What is the role of nitric oxide bioavailability in reflex blood pressure buffering?

Older men and women with hypertension will be randomly assigned to receive either dietary nitrate supplementation (beetroot juice) or placebo for 8 weeks. Researchers will compare results obtained from the four different groups to determine if increasing nitric oxide bioavailability influences neural control of blood pressure differently between older men and older women with hypertension.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age: 60-85 years old
* Hypertension treated with antihypertensive medication(s) or untreated with office sitting blood pressure ≥130/80 mmHg

Exclusion Criteria:

* Cardiovascular, pulmonary, and neurological diseases
* Office sitting blood pressure ≥180/110 mmHg or secondary hypertension
* Being on ≥3 antihypertensive agents
* Chronic kidney disease or renal failure
* Uncontrolled diabetes mellitus
* Untreated moderate-severe obstructive sleep apnea
* Current substance abuse
* Current smoking/vaping
* Body mass index ≥ 45 kg/m2 or body mass ≥ 300 lbs
* Orthostatic intolerance or recurrent syncope
* Endurance-trained athletes
* Impaired cognitive function or diagnosed dementia
* Medications that cannot be discontinued during study that interfere with nitric oxide production or study outcomes
* History of gout
* Hormone replacement therapy
